statement: The CCDR says climatic pressures could widen rural-urban and north-south gaps, compounding northern insecurity and displacement, including Sahelian in-migration.
compact_statement: The CCDR says climatic pressures could widen rural-urban and north-south gaps, compounding northern insecurity and displacement, including Sahelian in-migration.
affected_groups: People exposed to insecurity in northern Benin
scenario: No scenario or numeric horizon specified.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 18 (one-based), paragraph beginning ‘Climatic pressures are set to aggravate’.

uncertainty: Stated risk pathway; no causal estimate or displacement attribution.

statement: In EHCVM 2018/19, 21.4% of households reported a climate-induced shock during the previous three years; 10.5% reported flood impacts and 12% drought impacts.
compact_statement: In EHCVM 2018/19, 21.4% of households reported a climate-induced shock during the previous three years; 10.5% reported flood impacts and 12% drought impacts.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5, section 5.1.1, printed p. 51 (PDF p. 64), EHCVM 2018/19 household-shock paragraph.

uncertainty: Retrospective self-report; flood and drought shares may overlap.

statement: Poor, rural and agriculture-reliant households reported greater exposure to climate shocks; over 36% of agriculture-reliant households reported flood and/or drought impacts, versus about 21% overall.
compact_statement: Poor, rural and agriculture-reliant households reported greater exposure to climate shocks; over 36% of agriculture-reliant households reported flood and/or drought impacts, versus about 21% overall.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5, section 5.1.1, printed p. 51 (PDF p. 64), paragraphs on differential household impacts.

uncertainty: Historical self-report; subgroup differences are not causal estimates.

statement: The CCDR projects that by 2070, 98% of Benin’s territory could face extreme temperatures under a 2.7°C global-warming pathway associated with current policies.
compact_statement: The CCDR projects that by 2070, 98% of Benin’s territory could face extreme temperatures under a 2.7°C global-warming pathway associated with current policies.
scenario: 2.7°C global warming under current policies, as stated in the CCDR passage.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 1, section 1.2, printed p. 5 (PDF p. 18), projected extreme-temperature exposure paragraph.

uncertainty: Modelled exposure, not an observed temperature impact; retain the CCDR’s stated global-warming pathway.

statement: The World Bank summary says average annual GDP losses from climate change could reach up to 19% by 2050 without additional adaptation.
compact_statement: The World Bank summary says average annual GDP losses from climate change could reach up to 19% by 2050 without additional adaptation.
scenario: Without additional adaptation; the inspected summary does not specify the underlying climate scenario.

source_refs.locator: Publisher summary, bullet on projected climate-related economic losses.

uncertainty: Summary-level projection; underlying assumptions and uncertainty range were not available in the inspected passage.

statement: The NDC reports that agriculture employs about 70% of the population and accounts for 72.9% of export receipts; it identifies rainfall extremes, floods, dry spells, heat and strong winds as risks and lists 30 sectoral plus 51 commune-led adaptation projects.
compact_statement: The NDC reports that agriculture employs about 70% of the population and accounts for 72.9% of export receipts; it identifies rainfall extremes, floods, dry spells, heat and strong winds as risks and lists 30 sectoral plus 51 commune-led adaptation projects.

source_refs.locator: Section 3, agriculture subsection, printed pp. 14–15 (PDF pp. 14–15), paragraphs on sector profile and CDN 3.0 projects.

uncertainty: Economic figures refer to the period stated in the NDC; project counts describe plans, not completed or effective measures.

statement: The NDC identifies 30 communes in the coastal zone, five on the seafront, and reports shoreline retreat of 12–30 metres per year at critical points alongside flood, drought, wind and sea-level risks.
compact_statement: The NDC identifies 30 communes in the coastal zone, five on the seafront, and reports shoreline retreat of 12–30 metres per year at critical points alongside flood, drought, wind and sea-level risks.

source_refs.locator: Section 5.1.3, Littoral, printed pp. 51–52 (PDF pp. 49–50), coastal-risk description.

uncertainty: The erosion rate is reported for critical points, not as a uniform rate along the coast.
